| tool | wall (N = 1,000,000, spread batch) |
|---|---:|
| eagle.simulate (eagle picks the launch mode) | 48.9 ms |
| Warp per-thread kernel | 113 ms |
| PyTorch with torch.compile | 811 ms |
| JAX jit(vmap(while_loop)) | 1.24 s |
| CuPy masked | 9.34 s |

- **Tensor libraries compute every sample, every step** -- a masked array keeps computing the samples that already finished.
- **hawk + eagle skips finished samples** and packs the live ones into the next launch, so the batch keeps shrinking as samples finish.
- **Warp is excellent at per-thread kernels**: on a fully dense batch eagle.simulate beats it: 40.8 ms against Warp's 55.1 ms -- complementary tools, not a hierarchy.

RAPTOR adds, from the same source: per-sample Python, device-side stopping, forward- and reverse-mode derivatives, and the identical kernel on the CPU.

*Measured on NVIDIA H100 NVL. [Every number, every arm](https://amasat01.github.io/eagle/content/performance.html).*
